mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time when UNRATE is below 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates tighter monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and consumer spending potentially decreases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 60% of the time when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is growing, it indicates a strong labor market, which is likely to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time when both conditions are met, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) growth, defined as a year-over-year increase of less than 2%, may signal supply chain issues or reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time when INDPRO growth is below 2%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth, as indicated by GDPC1, above a 2% annualized rate suggests strong economic demand, which is likely to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) value, above 320, indicates strong inflationary pressures, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as the Federal Reserve may increase interest rates to combat inflation.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time when CPIAUCSL exceeds 320, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) are growing, it indicates strong consumer demand, which is likely to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time when both conditions are met, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime, when the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high, it may signal impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time when both conditions are met, this hypothesis is rejected.
